title: EDID (Extended Display Identification Data)
summary: EDID is a 128-byte (or 256-byte for EDID 1.4) data structure that describes a display's capabilities. Transmitted over DDC (Display Data Channel) on VGA/HDMI/DP. Contains: manufacturer ID (2 bytes, PNP ID), product code (2 bytes), serial number (4 bytes), manufacture week/year (2 bytes), EDID version/revision (2 bytes), video input params (1 byte), screen size (2 bytes), gamma (1 byte), features (1 byte), color characteristics (10 bytes), established timings (3 bytes), standard timings (16 bytes), detailed timings (4 x 18 bytes = 72 bytes), extension flag (1 byte), checksum (1 byte).

ext.summary: EDID is a 128-byte (or 256-byte for EDID 1.4) data structure that describes a display's capabilities. Transmitted over DDC (Display Data Channel) on VGA/HDMI/DP. Contains: manufacturer ID (2 bytes, PNP ID), product code (2 bytes), serial number (4 bytes), manufacture week/year (2 bytes), EDID version/revision (2 bytes), video input params (1 byte), screen size (2 bytes), gamma (1 byte), features (1 byte), color characteristics (10 bytes), established timings (3 bytes), standard timings (16 bytes), detailed timings (4 x 18 bytes = 72 bytes), extension flag (1 byte), checksum (1 byte).

structure.meaning: PNP ID (3 letters, 5 bits each, big-endian). E.g., 'DEL' = Dell.
Week (1 byte) + year (1 byte, years since 1990).
Version (1 byte) + revision (1 byte). E.g., 1.3 or 1.4.
DPMS (standby/suspend/active off), RGB color, display type, sRGB, preferred timing.
Chromaticity coordinates for red, green, blue, white.
Bitmap of supported standard timings (640x480@60, 800x600@60, 1024x768@60, etc.).
4 detailed timing descriptors (pixel clock, H/V active/blanking, sync offsets, etc.).
Number of extension blocks (each 128 bytes). 0x00 = no extensions.

ext.example_hex: 00 ff ff ff ff ff ff 00
notes: EDID is used by HDMI, DisplayPort, DVI, and VGA.
EDID extension blocks (CEA-861) carry HDR, audio, and color space info.
EDID can be overridden (custom EDID) for compatibility.
DisplayID is the successor to EDID (VESA DisplayID).
EDID is read by the GPU/OS to determine supported resolutions and timings.
